titulo: Amazon CEO pay ratio: $212.7M vs a $32,855 median worker
caption:
Amazon CEO pay ratio: $212.7M vs a $32,855 median worker

Amazon CEO pay ratio: the proxy statement says $212,701,169 for the CEO and $32,855 for the median worker. From the archive (Apr 2022), not today's news.
A proxy statement is the yearly filing a public company sends shareholders. Amazon's, dated April 14, 2022, reported its CEO's 2021 total pay as $212,701,169 and the median employee's 2021 total pay as $32,855. "Median" means the worker in the exact middle of the pay line: half earn more, half earn less.

The same document said: "committed to the safety and well-being of our employees" (Amazon, proxy statement).
The math: $212.7 million CEO total pay (2021) ÷ $32,855 median worker = about 6,474. That is the CEO pay ratio: CEO pay per median worker's annual pay. The proxy states the ratio as 1-to-6,474; the division gives 6,473.94, shown as 6,474.
How much does Amazon pay its workers? Per this filing, the median total pay worldwide, full-time and part-time, permanent and temporary, excluding the CEO, was $32,855 for 2021.
Why is the CEO number so big? Nearly all of the $212,701,169 is one restricted stock unit award, granted on the CEO's promotion and vesting over 10 years, per the proxy. It is stock, not a cash paycheck.

Committed to employees, it said. Here is the pay column. (Our take.)
